context: Single scatterplot of 1,500 synthetic researchers plotting years of experience vs. research publications, colored by 5 academic fields (Biology, Physics, Computer Science, Economics, Chemistry) with keyboard navigation and a toggle-able data table.
first_impression: The overall positive correlation reads clearly and the five-color palette is distinguishable at a glance, but dense overlap in the mid-experience range (10–20 years) creates a muddy center where field attribution becomes guesswork without interaction.
what_works: Five-color Tol bright palette stays within the cognitive threshold and hues are perceptually distinct enough to read the legend in under 3 seconds; single-view layout with no competing panels keeps working memory demand minimal.
what_doesnt: At 45% alpha with 1,500 points, the central cluster blends all five colors into an indistinguishable mass — per-field trends cannot be parsed without hover/keyboard interaction; the yellow (Economics) and cyan (Chemistry) dots are particularly hard to separate when stacked.
